description.value:
⚔ AURABLADE — MECHANICAL CORE (PHASE 1.5)

Emotion is not flavor text.
Emotion is a resource.

🔥 Burn — What It Is (Plainly)

Burn represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Burn is not a die pool.
Burn is a state track that unlocks power and risk.

You do not “spend” Burn.
You enter Burn states, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Gain Burn (Concrete Triggers)

You gain 1 Burn when any one of the following occurs:

Universal Burn Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You force a defense check using an Aura feature

  • You escalate without pause (GM-flagged high-risk continuation)

  • You remain in the same Aura for too long without stabilizing

⚠️ Limit:
You can gain at most 1 Burn per round, unless a subclass explicitly overrides this.

Burn rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Burn States (Explicit Bands)

Burn is divided into three states.

🔹 Burn 0–1 — Controlled

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Burn 2–3 — Engaged

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit 5E effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Burn 4+ — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

At this state:

  • Aura effects intensify

  • GM is authorized to:

    • Trigger backlash

    • Apply collateral

    • Force Aura collapse on a bad roll or narrative beat

This is the danger state.

🔥 What Happens at Backlash (Clear, Bounded)

When backlash triggers (GM discretion or subclass feature):

One of the following occurs (GM chooses or rolls):

  • You take psychic or sephirotic damage (radiant)

  • You suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on your next attack or save

  • Your Aura collapses (you drop to Burn 0)

  • A narrative consequence occurs (fear, escalation, attention)

Aurablades are not punished randomly.
They are punished predictably.

💠 AURA STATES — EXPLICIT MECHANICAL EFFECTS

Each Aura grants:

  • A passive effect

  • Engaged Burn effects

  • Overheated Burn effects

These are not manifestations.
They are combat permissions.

🔥 FURY — Escalation & Force

Theme: Press harder. Break lines.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to damage rolls with melee weapon attacks

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

When you hit with a melee attack:

  • Deal +tier damage

  • You may push the target 1 square or cleave a second creature within reach (once per turn)

You may also:

  • Ignore roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one attack per turn

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target must succeed on a Violence check or be knocked prone

  • Your attacks deny reactions until the start of your next turn

⚠️ Risk:

  • On a missed attack, GM may trigger backlash

Fury trades control for dominance.

🛡 RESOLVE — Defense & Refusal

Theme: Stand firm. Make removal expensive.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to Guard while you have not moved this turn

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

You may:

  • Gain resistance to one damage type until the start of your next turn

  • Ignore forced movement up to 2 squares

Additionally:

  • Opportunity attacks against you are made at disadvantage

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Automatically succeed on one Violence, Body, or Intrigue check per round

  • Lock your position: enemies cannot move you at all

⚠️ Risk:

  • When damage is fully negated, backlash may occur

Resolve dares the world to try harder.

🤍 MERCY — Protection & Restraint

Theme: Prevent loss. Redirect harm.

Passive (Always On)

  • You may choose to deal nonlethal damage without penalty

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

Once per round, when an ally within 2 squares takes damage:

  • Reduce that damage by tier

  • You may redirect it to yourself

You may also:

  • Automatically stabilize a creature you touch

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Prevent an ally from dropping below 1 Integrity (once per round)

  • Convert a failed last stand check into a success

⚠️ Risk:

  • Preventing death may trigger backlash or Aura collapse

Mercy delays consequences — it does not erase them.

🕳 DREAD — Suppression & Collapse

Theme: Remove hope. End momentum.

Passive (Always On)

  • Enemies within 1 square suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on morale-based checks (GM adjudication)

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

On hit:

  • Target must save or be Shaken until the end of its next turn

  • Target cannot take reactions

You may also:

  • Suppress one buff or inspiration effect (GM adjudication)

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target suffers roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on all saves until the start of your next turn

  • Nearby enemies must save or hesitate (lose movement or reactions)

⚠️ Risk:

  • Collateral fear or narrative fallout is likely

Dread does not kill bodies.
It kills belief.

🔄 Changing Aura (Explicit Rule)

You may change your Aura:

  • As a bonus action

  • Or as part of a rest or narrative reset

Changing Aura:

  • Does not clear Burn automatically

  • May reduce Burn by 1 if done defensively or narratively

Frequent swapping = control
Deep commitment = power

🧠 How Players Should Think About Aurablade

Ask yourself every turn:

  • “Do I escalate — or stabilize?”

  • “Can I afford another Burn?”

  • “What happens if this goes wrong?”

Aurablades are not forgiving.

They are honest.

The wound is the prayer.

Mode: Martyr · Drift: Toward

Blood Hymn Aurablades convert suffering into amplification. Where the base class governs Burn and Aura, the Hymn turns each blow into fuel — for cleave, for fear, for irreversible certainty. Played as the operative who runs toward the worst version of the fight on purpose.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Escalation. Your Burn feeds itself. While at Burn 2–3 (Engaged), weapon attacks deal +tier damage and grant +1 Burn (once per turn). At Burn 4+ (Overheated), the bonus scales further.
  • Level 6 — Lifetithe. Convert flesh into certainty. As part of an attack or Aura effect, take self-damage equal to your tier to gain +1 Burn (no action), reroll one damage die, or reclaim a previously expended Aura effect this turn.
  • Level 10 — Crimson Arc. Your violence spills outward. Once per turn, when you hit at Burn 2+, choose another creature within reach and deal half the original damage to them. At Burn 4+ the secondary target takes full damage and both must check against an additional rider.
  • Level 14 — Terror Charge. Fear trails behind you. While at Burn 3+, creatures you hit save or become Shaken; Shaken creatures suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on opportunity attacks against you and have reduced movement when fleeing. At Burn 4+ nearby allies of your target are also affected.
  • Level 18 — Final Crescendo (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, as a bonus action: enter Burn 4 immediately. For the rest of the turn, all attacks deal maximum damage and you may cleave freely (no once-per-turn limit). Aftermath: your Burn drops to 0 and you suffer severe backlash.

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Gridbreakers.

“Everything broken still remembers how it worked.”

Gridbreakers treat dead cities like sleeping machines. They know how to pry power from broken substations, wake lights in abandoned towers, and make a ruin choose sides. Where others see debris, they see leverage.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Investigation and the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Economy OPs.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Goetic Summoner.

“I have friends. They’re just… contractual.”

Goetic Summoners do not worship. They do not submit. They negotiate.

To a Goetic, the Great Work is not merely a path of purification. It is a war over leverage. Power exists in the Shatterlands, and much of it has teeth, names, appetites, and terms. If you can name it, you can sometimes bind it. If you can bind it, you can make it useful. For a while.

Goetics build circles, memorize taboos, track debts, and turn predatory forces into temporary infrastructure. They call this control. The world calls it an incident report waiting to happen.

How Goetics pursue the Great Work:

  • By extracting leverage from Qliphothic forces instead of merely resisting them
  • By binding hazards into assets and paying the price later
  • By treating Darkness as a resource with teeth
  • By weaponizing fear, coercion, and forbidden access where cleaner traditions would hesitate

Resonance: Qliphoth / Shadow — rupture, appetite, inversion, and the dangerous intelligence inside corruption.

Tell-tales: counted names, precise circles, a room that feels like it already agreed to terms before anyone spoke.

Faction Effects (Passive):

  • +1 to Violence OP rolls
  • +1 to Intrigue OP rolls

Cost Principle: every Goetic gain creates obligation. Expect Debt, escalating Darkness pressure, hostile notice, and consequences that remember your name longer than you wanted them to.

Tier 1 — Gridbreakers

“Everything broken still remembers how it worked.”

Gridbreakers treat dead cities like sleeping machines. They know how to pry power from broken substations, wake lights in abandoned towers, and make a ruin choose sides. Where others see debris, they see leverage.

You’ve learned the first law of a dead city: if it still sparks, it still negotiates.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Investigation and the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic: In Ruins or Urban Wreckage hexes, salvage and material recovery are easier and more reliable.

Tier 1 — Goetic Summoner

“First lesson: the circle protects you. Second lesson: only if it’s perfect.”

You learn the etiquette of predators: names, constraints, and the price of eye contact. You are not yet strong enough to command, but you are strong enough to be heard.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Occult and Intimidation
  • Learn Find Familiar, flavored as unsettling, watchful, or veil-adjacent

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • When your faction attempts intimidation, coercion, or violent leverage, gain +1 to the relevant Violence OP roll
  • When your faction runs reconnaissance, blackmail, or covert acquisition, gain +1 to the relevant Intrigue OP roll
  • When your faction attempts goodwill, legitimacy, or mass Diplomacy, suffer –1 to the relevant Soft Power OP roll

Cost: early Goetic work leaves an obvious scent. Expect attention from the wrong entities, fear from the right people, and a reputation that arrives before you do.

Heavy work jacket, reinforced gloves, and a thigh-strap of tool loops. The standard kit for hex-laborers, salvage crews, scrap-line foremen, and anyone whose day involves both sharp edges and difficult conversations with their employer. Not glamorous. Hard to ruin.

Standard Issue. Counts as armor for protection rolls and as gear for any skill check you can talk your way into calling "work."

manifestation.concept: A crown of shadow and refused mercy that hangs unseen above your head. Those who meet your eyes feel they have been judged.
manifestation.durationText: Persistent until you remove the crown — which only you can do.
manifestation.riskText: Allies stop volunteering information. Lovers report your sleep is troubled. Pets run.
manifestation.pathResonance: Aurablade — when the edge is worn instead of swung.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You walk into rooms and the rooms reorganize themselves around your presence.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-2 Form. Always-on; impossible to mask except by deliberate effort. Affects social rolls in both directions.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Once per scene, impose disadvantage (reroll-highest) on a Resolve check made within Near range.
manifestation.signature: Animals will not approach you. Children stop crying when you enter the room.
manifestation.thirdThing: Once a scene, you may name a single fear out loud — the room temperature drops a degree and your target hears it from the inside of their own thoughts.

system.effect: Call a blade of warm judgment into being. On a clean hit, the edge may cut flesh, fear, or a hostile binding—GM tunes which layer yields first.
system.flavor: A sunrise-thin blade runs with liquid gold and the smell of rain on hot stone.

manifestation.concept: A blade of compassionate force that punishes panic and cuts loose malignant attachment.
manifestation.costText: 1 Burn to call the blade. The edge is emotion given geometry.
manifestation.durationText: Persists for the scene or until dismissed.
manifestation.triggerText: It brightens when someone chooses courage at cost.
manifestation.targetText: One foe, one binding, or one fear-laden obstacle within reach.
manifestation.rangeAreaText: Reach 1; may also be laid across a threshold as a warning.
manifestation.riskText: If called in cruelty rather than conviction, the blade feeds the wielder's shame instead of their aim.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You may duel panic, sever malign tethers, and answer fear with visible resolve.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tune whether the cut lands on body, bond, curse, or mood. Keep it sharp, not universal.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Radiant melee manifestation; can threaten both integrity and hostile supernatural ties in the fiction.
manifestation.signature: Light gathers along the edge like a patient sunrise.
manifestation.thirdThing: The blade always leaves the smell of rain on hot stone.

system.flavor: Witness her unsheathe the brand and you witness exactly what she will not forgive.

manifestation.concept: A blade made of your conviction, hot to the touch and visibly upset.
manifestation.durationText: Until the scene ends or you sheath your fury.
manifestation.maintenanceCost: 1 Stress per scene maintained past the first.
manifestation.riskText: If you spend a turn calm, the brand fades and must be re-forged. If you betray the wrong it answers, it cuts you instead.
manifestation.pathResonance: Aurablade — fury chosen well, channeled cleanly.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You hold a weapon people can see, fear, and recognize as yours alone.
manifestation.gmCalibration: A Tier-1 Form. Visible to anyone in the room. Cannot be hidden, smuggled, or ambushed-with.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: On a hit, target gains the Burning condition for 1 round.
manifestation.signature: The edge sings the name of the wrong it answers.
manifestation.thirdThing: When you kill with it, the body's clothes scorch the precise sin into the cloth.

Sephirotic Scion. Your blood remembers the higher spheres. Light hangs around you a little too long, prayers sometimes answer themselves, and the world’s moral architecture feels less like an abstraction and more like the weather report.

Sephirotic Scion Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Sephirotic).

  • Size. You are Medium.

  • Speed. Your walking speed is 6 squares

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Sephirotic Scion does not grant any attribute bonuses.

Your Sephirotic heritage grants you additional features through advancements (Item Grants) added during character creation: sephirotic physiology, attunement to higher patterns, holy conduction, the Light of Harmony, and strategic hooks that tilt factions toward soft power, diplomacy, and alignment work.

Sefirot Attunement. You perceive the harmonic structure beneath events.

  • You gain a bonus to Perception checks and passive Perception.
  • Your intuition occasionally warns you about moral or spiritual imbalances (GM discretion).

Holy Conduit. Your body routes excess metaphysical charge safely.

  • You have resistance to psychic damage.
  • Your presence stabilizes magically turbulent areas.
  • Bad Eden engines treat you as a low-level metaphysical conductor (see world logic).

“You glow a little. Sometimes metaphorically. Sometimes not.”

  • You can cast calm emotions 1/Soma Break (Presence is your manifestation aptitude).
  • Allies within 2 squares reroll the lowest die on checks against being frightened.
  • You automatically sense the Sephirothic/Qliphothic tilt of any hex you enter.

Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Sephirotic Scion heritage: Ophanic.

“The wheels were full of eyes. You never stop turning. You never stop seeing.”

Sephirotic Scion (Ophanic). Your blood runs rotating. The Ophanim are wheels-and-eyes — motion, sight, the order that is always already looking both ways. You are descended from a thing that could not be snuck up on because it had no back. You kept some of that. Not all. Enough.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Sephirotic Scion).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Sephirotic Scion does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Intrigue in fiction and through Tier powers.

Sephirotic Scion Core: The Higher Register

Shared across all Sephirotic Scion heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Sephirotic Physiology. You have resistance to sephirotic damage. Your blood runs a little bright under the right light; you do not technically age while on consecrated ground.

  • Sefirot Attunement. At creation, pick one sephirah (player choice). Once per scene, you can invoke its register and gain a +1 rank bonus to one check that falls clearly within that sephirah's domain.

  • Holy Conduit. Manifestations, rituals, and other sephirotic-register effects that target you or pass through your space treat their effective caster-attribute as +1 for the duration of that effect. Works on allies and on you; does not work on qliphothic-register effects.

  • Light of Harmony. When two or more creatures within 6 squares of you are in active, explicit agreement (stated aloud), they each gain 1 temporary Integrity. This refreshes when a new agreement is reached between different creatures.

Ophanic Traits

  • Wheel-and-Eye. You can see invisible creatures and objects within 6 squares as dimly lit shapes. You cannot be flanked.

  • Concentric Sight. You reroll the lowest die on Mind (Perception) checks that involve noticing movement, pattern, or change over time. You roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Mind (Perception) checks to notice things that have been perfectly still since before you started looking — you see motion, not furniture.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +2 Intrigue OP and +1 Violence OP at campaign start.

  • Hex Synergy. In Battlefield / Procession / High-Traffic hexes, your faction's observation and counter-intel operations gain +2 on the success check.

  • Turning Witness. Once per Strategic Turn, you may observe one exchange of goods, intelligence, or personnel between two rival factions within your field of influence. You learn that it happened and between whom, though not necessarily what was exchanged.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Sefirot Attunement Recovery: 1/scene  ·  Action: Free (declare before roll)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. Invoke your chosen sephirah for +1 rank bonus on a check clearly in its domain.

members.name: Sklar Brask
members.notes: Wrote the whole thing down so it couldn't be forgotten or fixed. Owes you a round at the Salt House and keeps saying next visit.

members.name: Sklar Halloran
members.notes: Learned a song that quiets bound things and only sings it when needed; respects you the way a smith respects a flaw they can't quite hammer out.

members.name: Knox Holt
members.notes: Shared a long quiet job with you once; you've trusted each other ever since; once kept the lights on in Port Kudzu when the grid died.

members.name: Marn Mott
members.notes: Still thinks you were wrong about the job, and is still right; once broke a long peace with one sentence and rebuilt it with twelve.

members.name: Bram Ketch
members.notes: Writes you whenever they hear about a working printer — took the rap for a friend and got out a year early on good behavior.

members.name: Wren Saltmouth
members.notes: Can fix anything with a wire and a patient hour; swore they'd never work with you again, and keeps showing up; took the long winter watching the Lattice for changes no one believed in.
